world.title: US strikes hit Iran for seventh consecutive night
world.summary: The United States has conducted strikes against Iran for the seventh consecutive night, with Iran retaliating against US allies in the region. Kuwait reported that a power and water plant was hit in Iranian attacks. The escalating military operations represent a significant intensification of US-Iran tensions in the Middle East, with both sides conducting coordinated strikes. Iran has claimed that three people were killed in US strikes, while the US military states its operations aim to degrade Iran's military capabilities. The strikes have also triggered alarm in neighboring countries, with sirens reported in Bahrain as regional tensions continue to mount.

world.title: Trump threatens new Canada tariffs over fires sending 'filthy' air into US cities
world.summary: US President Trump has threatened to impose new tariffs on Canada in response to wildfires sending smoke into American cities, characterizing the air quality as 'filthy.' Canadian leader Mark Carney countered that both nations share equal responsibility for addressing climate change, which experts say is worsening wildfire conditions. The dispute highlights tensions between the two countries over environmental management and trade policy. Trump's tariff threat represents an escalation of trade tensions between the US and Canada, while Canadian officials emphasize the shared nature of climate-related challenges affecting air quality across North America.

world.title: Many Ukrainian soldiers outraged over removal of defence minister, troops tell BBC
world.summary: Ukrainian soldiers have expressed outrage following the removal of Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov, with protests erupting across the country on Thursday. Military personnel have joined civilians in criticizing the government's decision to dismiss the defence minister. The controversy reflects internal tensions within Ukraine's military and political leadership during the ongoing conflict with Russia. Soldiers' dissatisfaction with the removal suggests concerns about military strategy and leadership decisions. The incident highlights divisions within Ukraine's defense establishment at a critical time, with troops questioning the wisdom of removing a key military figure during wartime operations.

world.title: Space start-up launches India's first commercial rocket designed for orbit
world.summary: India's space-tech unicorn Skyroot Aerospace successfully launched Vikram-1, marking India's first commercial rocket designed for orbital missions. The launch represents a significant milestone for India's private space industry and demonstrates the country's growing capabilities in commercial spaceflight. Skyroot Aerospace's achievement reflects India's expanding role in the global commercial space sector, competing with established international players. The successful Vikram-1 launch opens new possibilities for India's satellite deployment and space commerce opportunities. This development positions India as an emerging player in the competitive commercial space market, potentially enabling domestic and international clients to access affordable launch services.

world.title: Magnitude 7.3 earthquake quake strikes off Mexico coast
world.summary: A magnitude 7.3 earthquake struck off the coast of Mexico, generating tsunami waves recorded by the US Tsunami Warning Center. Waves measuring 0.3 meters (1.1 feet) high were recorded in Puerto Madero and Chiapas regions following the seismic event. The earthquake represents a significant natural disaster affecting Mexico's Pacific coastal areas. The tsunami waves, while relatively modest in height, indicate the earthquake's substantial underwater displacement. Authorities monitored the situation closely to assess potential damage and ensure public safety in affected coastal communities along Mexico's Pacific seaboard.

usa.title: What to know about the Canadian and US wildfires and their impact
usa.summary: Wildfires in Ontario have blanketed US and Canadian cities with dangerous smoke, creating hazardous air quality conditions across multiple regions. The smoke poses significant health risks to millions of people, with air pollution levels reaching record highs in dozens of US cities. Canadian leader Mark Carney emphasizes that both nations share equal responsibility for addressing climate change, which experts say is worsening wildfire conditions. President Trump has threatened new tariffs against Canada over the smoke affecting US cities. The situation highlights the transnational nature of environmental crises and the need for coordinated international response to both immediate air quality threats and underlying climate factors driving increased wildfire severity.

usa.title: At least two dead in Texas floods ravaging same area where campers died
usa.summary: Texas is experiencing devastating floods that are striking the same region devastated by floods last year, which caused more than 130 deaths. The recurring disaster in the same area raises concerns about infrastructure resilience and disaster preparedness in flood-prone regions. At least two deaths have been reported from the current flooding event, with officials warning of continued dangerous conditions. The repeated impact on the same community within a year highlights vulnerabilities in flood management and recovery efforts. This pattern of recurring natural disasters in identical locations underscores the need for improved infrastructure investments, early warning systems, and comprehensive disaster mitigation strategies to protect residents from repeated catastrophic events.

usa.title: Taco Bell removes lettuce from menu in US after links to explosive diarrhoea parasite
usa.summary: Taco Bell has removed lettuce from its US menu following a parasite outbreak linked to the fast-food chain. Approximately 1,645 people across five states were infected by the parasite after consuming Taco Bell products, according to US health officials. The outbreak prompted the company to take immediate action to prevent further infections and restore consumer confidence in food safety. The incident highlights vulnerabilities in the fresh produce supply chain and the importance of rigorous food safety protocols. A Central Coast farm company has been linked to the national outbreak, raising questions about agricultural practices and quality control measures. The removal of lettuce represents a significant operational change for the restaurant chain and underscores ongoing challenges in ensuring the safety of fresh produce from farm to consumer.

usa.title: Trump alleges China meddled in 2020 election and questions voting security ahead of midterms
usa.summary: President Trump has alleged that China interfered in the 2020 election and raised questions about voting security ahead of November's midterm elections. China has dismissed Trump's claims as fabricated, while US Democrats argue he is laying groundwork to undermine the legitimacy of the upcoming elections. Election experts have stated that Trump's speech and released unclassified documents provide no evidence supporting his allegations. The claims reflect ongoing partisan disputes over election integrity and voting security in the United States. Trump's statements come amid broader concerns about election security and foreign interference, though officials emphasize the robustness of US voting systems. The controversy highlights the contentious political environment surrounding elections and the challenge of distinguishing between legitimate security concerns and partisan rhetoric.

usa.title: US data center protests go national as backlash grows
usa.summary: Opponents of rapid data center expansion are organizing coordinated protests across the United States, with demonstrations planned for Saturday in at least 125 locations. This marks the first national effort to channel growing anger at the accelerated buildout of artificial intelligence infrastructure over the past year. The expansion of data centers has roiled local politics and sparked significant community backlash in numerous regions. Protesters are concerned about various impacts including energy consumption, environmental effects, land use, and local community disruption. The nationwide coordination demonstrates the scale of opposition to AI infrastructure development and reflects broader public concerns about the pace and consequences of technological expansion. The protests represent a significant grassroots movement challenging corporate and government priorities regarding data center development and its effects on communities.

india.title: Diamonds and 'cab to orbit': Rocket aiming to transform India's space ambitions takes off
india.summary: India's first privately developed orbital rocket, Vikram-1, successfully launched by space-tech unicorn Skyroot Aerospace on Saturday, placing multiple payloads into low-Earth orbit. The vehicle utilized advanced carbon-composite structures and a restartable liquid-fuelled module, marking a significant milestone in opening India's space sector to private companies. This successful mission validates India's capabilities in private orbital launch vehicle development and demonstrates the country's growing commercial space industry, potentially transforming India's space ambitions through private sector participation.

india.title: Sonam Wangchuk forcibly taken to hospital after 20 days of hunger strike
india.summary: Activist Sonam Wangchuk was forcibly hospitalized after conducting a 20-day hunger strike, continuing a tradition of protest through fasting in Indian politics. Following his hospitalization, Cockroach Janta Party founder Abhijeet Dipke began an indefinite fast in Wangchuk's place, demonstrating the ongoing significance of hunger strikes as political tools in India. This reflects a broader pattern where such protests have historically shaped Indian politics and policy outcomes, from Mahatma Gandhi's era to contemporary activism, highlighting how civil disobedience through fasting remains a powerful mechanism for political change and public attention.

india.title: Crackdown on 'objectionable' books in Indian-administered Kashmir sparks row
india.summary: Authorities in Indian-administered Kashmir have instructed educational institutions to review every book on their premises, raising concerns about censorship and freedom of expression. This crackdown on materials deemed 'objectionable' has sparked significant controversy among civil liberties advocates and educators. The directive represents a broader pattern of content regulation in the region and has generated debate about the balance between administrative authority and intellectual freedom in educational settings, with implications for students' access to diverse literary and academic materials.

india.title: Muslim judge in India faces death threats after convicting 'cow vigilantes'
india.summary: Judge Tabassum Khan has faced severe online abuse and death threats following her conviction of fourteen Hindu men in a lynching case related to cow vigilantism. The case highlights tensions surrounding communal violence and judicial independence in India, with the judge's religious identity becoming a focal point for harassment. This incident raises concerns about the safety of judicial officers who deliver verdicts in sensitive communal cases and reflects broader challenges regarding religious polarization, online harassment, and the protection of those administering justice in contentious matters.

india.title: India is adding biofuels to petrol – but many drivers are unhappy
india.summary: India has begun adding biofuels to petrol through the E20 fuel blend, a policy aimed at promoting renewable energy and reducing petroleum dependence. However, motorists have expressed significant dissatisfaction, reporting reduced fuel efficiency in their vehicles and concerns about potential higher maintenance costs. The implementation has generated consumer backlash despite environmental benefits, highlighting the tension between government sustainability goals and practical consumer concerns, raising questions about the transition strategy's effectiveness and public acceptance of green fuel initiatives.

odisha.title: Minor boy stripped, beaten in Cuttack. FIR filed after video goes viral
odisha.summary: A disturbing viral video documented a minor boy being stripped and physically assaulted in Cuttack's Chauliaganj area, sparking significant public outrage and immediate police intervention. The incident prompted authorities to file a First Information Report (FIR) following widespread circulation of the footage on social media platforms. Police have issued warnings against further sharing of material that identifies the victim, emphasizing the need to protect the child's privacy and dignity during the investigation. The case highlights growing concerns about violence against minors and the role of social media in exposing such crimes, while also raising questions about responsible sharing of sensitive content involving children.

sports.title: All Blacks punish Ireland in dominant Eden Park win
sports.summary: New Zealand's rugby team delivered a dominant performance against Ireland in a Nations Championship match at Eden Park, scoring five tries to secure a convincing victory. The result extends the All Blacks' remarkable 32-year unbeaten record at their home ground, demonstrating their continued dominance in international rugby. The match was largely one-sided, with New Zealand's ruthless attacking play overwhelming Ireland's defense throughout the contest, showcasing the All Blacks' status as a premier rugby nation.

sports.title: Clark makes history with 45 points and 10 assists
sports.summary: Caitlin Clark achieved a historic milestone in WNBA history by becoming the first player ever to record over 40 points and 10 assists in a single game. Playing for the Indiana Fever against the Seattle Storm, Clark's exceptional performance demonstrated her elite scoring and playmaking abilities at the professional level. This record-breaking achievement underscores Clark's emergence as one of the league's most dynamic and impactful players, capable of dominating games through both individual scoring and facilitating teammates' success.

sports.title: Sam Burns ties Open Championship round record with 62
sports.summary: Sam Burns equaled the record for the lowest round at a men's major championship, shooting a 62 during the second round of the 2026 Open Championship at Royal Birkdale. Burns' exceptional performance included a fantastic finish, holing out from a bunker on the 18th hole to secure his place in golf history alongside Lucas Herbert, who previously matched this record. The achievement highlights Burns' exceptional skill and composure under pressure in one of golf's most prestigious tournaments.

sports.title: Messi and Brady in disbelief over 'prophetic' Lamine Yamal photo
sports.summary: Lionel Messi expressed amazement at the coincidence of facing Spain's Lamine Yamal in the 2026 World Cup final, recalling a photograph taken when Yamal was a baby. The iconic image, which captured Messi holding the infant Yamal years earlier, has taken on prophetic significance as both players now meet on football's biggest stage. Messi described the situation as "crazy," highlighting the remarkable nature of their paths converging at this moment in their careers and the enduring legacy of that early encounter.

sports.title: The harrowing dark side of England's World Cup exit
sports.summary: Research reveals a disturbing correlation between England's World Cup participation and increased domestic abuse incidents, with women and girls living in constant fear during major football tournaments. The study highlights how major sporting events can have serious negative social consequences, particularly for vulnerable populations. This finding underscores the complex relationship between sports, national passion, and societal issues, demonstrating that while football captivates millions, it can simultaneously create dangerous conditions for those experiencing domestic violence during periods of heightened emotional intensity.

cricket.title: Garry Sobers dies, aged 89
cricket.summary: Sir Garfield Sobers, the legendary West Indies allrounder, has passed away at his home in Barbados at age 89. Sobers is widely regarded as one of cricket's greatest players, having revolutionized the sport with his exceptional all-round abilities as a batsman, bowler, and fielder. His death has prompted tributes from cricket figures worldwide, including Sir Geoffrey Boycott, who described him as a 'once-in-a-lifetime' player. Sobers' legacy extends beyond his on-field achievements, as he became a global ambassador for cricket and inspired generations of players across the sport.

cricket.title: Rohit Sharma's international future hangs in the balance
cricket.summary: India's selectors have informed 39-year-old captain Rohit Sharma that he is not part of the country's 2027 World Cup plans, casting uncertainty over his international future. However, BCCI secretary Devajit Saikia subsequently dismissed speculation about Sharma's ODI future, stating that the Lord's ODI against England will not be his last match. The situation highlights the ongoing transition in Indian cricket leadership as the team prepares for future tournaments. Sharma's potential retirement has generated significant discussion among cricket commentators, with figures like Kapil Dev suggesting his retirement should be celebrated when it occurs.

cricket.title: Washington out of India's third ODI against England
cricket.summary: India allrounder Washington Sundar has been ruled out of the third ODI against England due to a leg injury, creating an opportunity for Kuldeep Yadav to return to the squad. The injury to Washington leaves India needing to adjust their playing XI for the upcoming match, with Kuldeep positioned as the likely replacement. This development occurs during a significant ODI series between India and England, with both teams competing for series advantage. The injury situation highlights the ongoing challenges teams face in managing player fitness during intensive international cricket schedules.

cricket.title: Refreshed Knight Riders face usual suspects Freedom in MLC final
cricket.summary: The Knight Riders will face Freedom in the MLC final, with the Knight Riders seeking their first title in the competition. The Knight Riders benefit from a four-day gap before the final, which could prove pivotal in their preparation and recovery for the match. This break provides the team with valuable time to rest players, strategize, and address any fitness concerns ahead of the championship decider. The final represents a significant opportunity for the Knight Riders to claim their maiden MLC title, while Freedom will be looking to defend their status as established contenders in the tournament.

cricket.title: ODI World Cup Qualifier winner gains direct entry to 2027 main round
cricket.summary: The winner of the ODI World Cup Qualifier will gain direct entry to the 2027 World Cup main round, avoiding the Super Series stage. This qualification pathway represents a significant advantage, as the Super Series is designed to eliminate two of the four teams competing in that stage before the main World Cup tournament. The direct entry provides the qualifier winner with a substantial competitive advantage and reduces the risk of early elimination. This format change underscores the evolving structure of World Cup qualification, offering clearer pathways for emerging cricket nations to reach the main tournament stage.

usa_stock.title: SpaceX postponed a crucial launch — and its stock went on to close below IPO price for second day
usa_stock.summary: SpaceX shares declined approximately 4% in premarket trading following an aborted mission, marking the second consecutive day the stock closed below its initial public offering price of $135 per share. The postponement of the crucial launch has raised concerns among investors about the company's near-term operational capabilities and mission success rates. Despite the recent setback, analysts remain divided on the stock's long-term prospects, with some viewing the current valuation as presenting both risks and potential opportunities for investors willing to weather near-term volatility.

usa_stock.title: Chip stocks have entered a bear market. A BofA analyst says not to panic.
usa_stock.summary: The semiconductor sector has entered bear market territory, declining more than 20% from recent highs, with Bank of America analysts advising investors not to panic. The sector is undergoing a reset and historically tends to underperform during the third quarter. Despite the significant downturn, analysts suggest this correction may represent a healthy market consolidation rather than a fundamental deterioration in the industry's long-term prospects. Several semiconductor stocks remain up triple digits for the year despite July declines exceeding 25-30%.

usa_stock.title: Meet Kimi K3, the newest Chinese AI model haunting Silicon Valley
usa_stock.summary: Moonshot AI has unveiled Kimi K3, a new open-source artificial intelligence model that is rapidly catching up to leading American competitors Anthropic and OpenAI. The emergence of this advanced Chinese AI model is raising significant questions about the competitive dynamics and future trajectory of the global AI race. The development has sparked concerns among Silicon Valley investors and technology leaders about maintaining American technological leadership in artificial intelligence, a sector viewed as critical to long-term economic and strategic competitiveness.

usa_stock.title: The average stock is having a moment as semiconductors struggle. It's a sign of a healthy market.
usa_stock.summary: While semiconductor stocks have experienced significant declines, broader market dynamics show strength in average stocks across various sectors, suggesting a healthy market rotation. Energy companies have emerged as notable gainers, with the sector posting strong performance as investors reallocate capital away from struggling chip stocks. This divergence between semiconductor weakness and broader market strength indicates market participants are selectively rotating into different sectors, which analysts interpret as a sign of market health and normal portfolio rebalancing rather than systemic weakness.

usa_stock.title: 19 (mostly) tech stocks that have fallen at least 25% in July
usa_stock.summary: Nineteen technology stocks have experienced declines of at least 25% during July 2026, reflecting significant sector-wide volatility and investor repositioning. Notably, seven of the worst-performing stocks for the month remain up by triple digits for the full year, indicating that despite sharp July pullbacks, many technology companies have maintained substantial year-to-date gains. This pattern suggests that recent declines represent profit-taking and sector rotation rather than fundamental deterioration in company valuations or long-term growth prospects.

ai.title: Meet GPT-Red: an LLM super-hacker OpenAI built to make its models safer
ai.summary: OpenAI has developed GPT-Red, an advanced language model designed to function as a security testing tool. The system acts as a sparring partner to help other OpenAI models strengthen their defenses against cyberattacks and vulnerabilities. OpenAI integrated GPT-Red into the training process for GPT-5.6, its latest flagship model, which the company claims is now its most robust release to date. GPT-Red automates the identification of potential security weaknesses, enabling more comprehensive adversarial testing than traditional methods. This approach represents a significant advancement in AI safety practices, demonstrating how AI systems can be leveraged to improve the security and resilience of other AI models against emerging threats.

ai.title: What Anthropic's latest AI discovery does—and doesn't—show
ai.summary: Anthropic, valued at nearly $1 trillion and recognized as the world's most valuable AI company, has published research revealing new insights into how AI models process information internally. The company announced it had discovered a window into its models' "internal thoughts" as they reason through answers to queries. This research contributes to Anthropic's broader mission of understanding AI behavior and safety. The company has gained a reputation for publishing unconventional research, including investigations into whether AI models can experience pain. These discoveries have significant implications for AI interpretability and safety, helping researchers better understand how large language models make decisions and potentially improving oversight of AI systems.

ai.title: PsiQuantum has a plan to make a massive quantum computer out of light
ai.summary: PsiQuantum has unveiled an ambitious plan to construct a large-scale quantum computer using photonic technology. The system will occupy a space resembling a hybrid between a data center and an ice cream factory, containing approximately 100 stainless-steel cabinets, each standing six feet tall. The cabinets will be connected to liquid helium cooling systems maintaining temperatures only a few degrees above absolute zero. This photonic approach represents a novel direction in quantum computing development, potentially offering advantages over traditional superconducting qubit systems. The project represents significant progress toward building practical, large-scale quantum computers that could revolutionize computational capabilities across multiple industries and scientific fields.

ai.title: The risk of weather data sabotage is rising
ai.summary: Weather forecasting data has become a critical infrastructure asset with significant economic and safety implications. Airline dispatchers, grid operators, and farmers worldwide rely on weather forecasts for major strategic decisions affecting real money, livelihoods, and lives. The increasing dependence on weather predictions for high-stakes operations creates vulnerability to potential data sabotage and manipulation. Compromised weather data could have cascading effects across multiple industries simultaneously. As weather forecasting systems become more integrated into critical infrastructure and decision-making processes, the security of these systems has become increasingly important. The article highlights emerging risks associated with the centralization and digitization of weather data, emphasizing the need for robust security measures to protect this essential information source.

ai.title: EU will force Google to share search data and open up AI on Android
ai.summary: European Union regulators have officially mandated that Google share search data and open its AI capabilities on the Android platform. This regulatory action represents a significant intervention in tech industry practices, requiring Google to provide greater access to its proprietary systems and data. Google has expressed concerns that these changes could compromise user privacy and security. The directive reflects broader EU efforts to promote competition and reduce the dominance of major technology companies in digital markets. These requirements will likely reshape how Google operates in Europe and may establish precedents for AI regulation globally. The mandate addresses concerns about market concentration and fair competition in search and mobile operating systems.

quantum.title: Quantum error correction can constantly recalibrate a processor
quantum.summary: Researchers have demonstrated that quantum error correction can continuously recalibrate quantum processors using reinforcement learning. The technique leverages error information to dynamically adjust control algorithms, improving processor performance. This advancement addresses a fundamental challenge in quantum computing: maintaining qubit stability and accuracy despite environmental interference and decoherence. By automating the recalibration process through machine learning, the approach could enhance the reliability and scalability of near-term quantum devices, bringing practical quantum computing applications closer to reality.

quantum.title: Thermodynamic Computers Go With the (Energy) Flow
quantum.summary: Researchers are exploring thermodynamic computers that harness random energy fluctuations rather than protecting against them as conventional computers do. Today's digital systems require safeguards to shield against thermal noise and energy variations that degrade performance. Thermodynamic computing inverts this paradigm, leveraging natural energy fluctuations as computational resources. This approach could fundamentally reduce power consumption and heat dissipation in computing systems. By working with thermodynamic principles instead of against them, these computers promise more efficient information processing aligned with physical laws governing energy and entropy.

quantum.title: An orbiting disco ball gave Einstein's theory its most precise test yet
quantum.summary: Scientists used an orbiting reflective sphere—resembling a disco ball—to conduct the most precise test of Einstein's general relativity theory to date. The experiment measured how Earth's mass distorts spacetime around the planet, confirming Einstein's predictions with unprecedented accuracy. Despite Earth's relatively modest mass compared to stellar objects, the planet still measurably warps the fabric of spacetime. This test validates fundamental aspects of general relativity using satellite-based laser ranging technology, demonstrating that even subtle gravitational effects predicted by Einstein's theory can be experimentally verified with modern precision instruments.

quantum.title: We Know Simple Fluids Can Flow. Turns Out, Some Can Fracture.
quantum.summary: Researchers have discovered that certain simple, nonelastic fluids can fracture and break apart, challenging long-held assumptions about fluid mechanics. Scientists previously believed that elasticity was the key property enabling complex fluids to fracture. However, observations of cracks forming in nonelastic simple fluids suggest a more nuanced understanding of fluid behavior. This finding prompts reconsideration of fundamental fluid dynamics principles and may have implications for materials science, industrial processes, and understanding natural phenomena. The discovery highlights gaps in current theoretical frameworks governing how fluids respond to stress and deformation.

quantum.title: Will We Ever Find Alien Civilizations?
quantum.summary: Astronomer David Kipping discusses the challenges in searching for extraterrestrial life and civilizations beyond Earth. He examines why many claims of alien life have dissolved under scientific scrutiny and advocates for more statistically rigorous approaches to the search for life beyond Earth. Kipping argues that current methodologies often lack sufficient grounding in probability and statistics, leading to overconfident conclusions. He presents a rational case for considering the possibility that humanity may be alone in the universe, emphasizing the importance of applying rigorous scientific standards to astrobiology research and reconsidering assumptions underlying the search for extraterrestrial intelligence.

trump.title: Trump alleges China meddled in 2020 election and questions voting security ahead of midterms
trump.summary: President Trump alleged that China interfered in the 2020 election and raised questions about voting security in advance of the upcoming midterm elections. China denied the allegations as fabricated, while US Democrats criticized Trump's claims, arguing he was laying groundwork to undermine the November elections. The statements reflect Trump's continued focus on election integrity concerns and represent a significant political development as the midterm campaign intensifies.

trump.title: Trump threatens new Canada tariffs over fires sending 'filthy' air into US cities
trump.summary: President Trump threatened to impose new tariffs on Canada in response to wildfires sending smoke into US cities, which he characterized as 'filthy' air. Canadian leader Mark Carney responded by stating that both nations share equal responsibility for combating climate change, which experts indicate is worsening wildfire conditions. The dispute highlights tensions between the two countries over environmental issues and trade policy, with Trump using tariff threats as leverage in the ongoing disagreement.

trump.title: Trump Media to sell instant access to 'market-moving' social posts
trump.summary: Trump Media is launching a premium paid feed providing Wall Street traders with instant access to the company's most influential social media posts, positioning them as 'market-moving' content. The service targets financial professionals seeking early access to potentially impactful announcements. This business development represents a new revenue stream for Trump Media and reflects the company's efforts to monetize its social platform by offering premium services to institutional investors and traders interested in real-time market-sensitive information.

trump.title: White House teleprompter operator accused of making $100k from Trump speech bets
trump.summary: A White House staffer has been accused of using inside knowledge of presidential speeches to generate nearly $100,000 in profits through betting on the Kalshi platform. The allegation raises serious concerns about potential insider trading and misuse of confidential government information for personal financial gain. The incident highlights security vulnerabilities within the White House and questions about oversight of staff access to sensitive information regarding the president's public statements and their potential market impact.

trump.title: Trump DHS using unverified figures to attack election officials on non-citizen voting
trump.summary: The Trump administration's Department of Homeland Security is escalating attacks on election officials in key battleground states, with Secretary Markwayne Mullin making claims that hundreds of thousands of non-citizens are illegally registered to vote. However, the agency has privately acknowledged these figures have not been fully vetted or verified. The controversy reflects ongoing partisan disputes over election integrity, with critics arguing the administration is using unsubstantiated claims to undermine confidence in election officials ahead of midterm elections.

local.title: Skokie, Illinois residents give village an earful in wake of water main flooding
local.summary: The Village of Skokie issued a declaration of emergency following significant water main flooding that affected residents. The emergency declaration is the first step in applying for state and county disaster funds. However, residents expressed concerns to CBS News Chicago about whether they would actually receive financial assistance from those funds. The water main incident prompted the village to take formal action to seek external aid for affected residents and infrastructure damage.

local_events.title: Wednesdays on the Green
local_events.summary: Weekly concert series presented by the Skokie Chamber of Commerce in cooperation with the Village of Skokie, Skokie Park District, and Skokie Public Library. Bring a folding chair.
local_events.source: The Village Green, Skokie (between Skokie Public Library and Skokie Village Hall)

local_events.title: Skokie Farmers Market
local_events.summary: Producers-only farmers market featuring vendors from Illinois, Indiana, Michigan, and Wisconsin selling locally grown and made products. Live music and free kids' activities accompany the market each weekend.

local_events.title: Let's Talk Veins Skokie | Free Vein Screening Event + Lunch
local_events.summary: Free vein screening event with lunch provided. Community health event offering vascular health screenings and information for Skokie residents.

local_events.title: Sound Bath Meditation
local_events.summary: Sound bath meditation event in Skokie offering relaxation and wellness through immersive sound therapy experience.

local_weather.title: Weather in Skokie, Illinois
local_weather.summary: Clear sky, 80°F (feels like 84°F). Today's range: 78°F to 81°F. Humidity 79%, wind 3 mph.
